nodes.label: Cache Components rules (cacheComponents: true)
nodes.rationale: Violating either constraint is a build error rather than a runtime bug, so the rules are enforced structurally: all reads in content.ts, perspective resolved above the cache boundary.

nodes.label: Cache tags must cover dereferenced types
nodes.norm_label: cache tags must cover dereferenced types
nodes.rationale: The revalidate webhook invalidates by _type and knows nothing about references, so a query that dereferences author-> must also be tagged with person or it goes stale.

nodes.label: Content comes from Sanity (no hardcoded copy)
nodes.norm_label: content comes from sanity (no hardcoded copy)
nodes.rationale: Any user-facing sentence must become a schema field so editors can change copy without a code deploy.

nodes.label: Headlines are Portable Text with accent marks
nodes.norm_label: headlines are portable text with accent marks
nodes.rationale: Lime marker / green / rust accents are marks rendered by components/sanity/Headline.tsx so editors can move emphasis without code changes; never split into partA+highlight+partB strings.

nodes.label: Never put a dot in a document _id
nodes.norm_label: never put a dot in a document _id
nodes.rationale: Sanity reads a dot as a path separator; path-prefixed documents are hidden from unauthenticated reads (same mechanism as drafts.*). The site fetches published content without a token, so a dotted ID renders in Studio but 404s for visitors. Use '-'.

nodes.label: PerspectiveGate route pattern (cookies above cache boundary)
nodes.norm_label: perspectivegate route pattern (cookies above cache boundary)
nodes.rationale: cookies()/headers() cannot be read inside 'use cache'; PerspectiveGate resolves the perspective above the boundary and threads it down as FetchOptions so it becomes part of the cache key. generateMetadata uses PUBLISHED directly to keep the document head in the static shell.

nodes.label: Numbering derived from array position
nodes.rationale: Numbers and anchors (legal sections, FAQ groups, funnel stages) are never stored so reordering in the Studio renumbers automatically.

nodes.label: sanityFetch only inside 'use cache' scope
nodes.rationale: sanityFetch calls cacheTag() and cacheLife() internally, which throw outside a cache scope; centralising call sites in sanity/lib/content.ts guarantees this.

nodes.label: Images via SanityImage with lqip + dimensions (IMAGE fragment)
nodes.norm_label: images via sanityimage with lqip + dimensions (image fragment)
nodes.rationale: SanityImage reads dimensions from the asset ref so next/image reserves space without a round trip; queries must project lqip and dimensions.

nodes.label: Never put a dot in a document _id (fix-dotted-ids)
nodes.norm_label: never put a dot in a document _id (fix-dotted-ids)
nodes.rationale: Dot is a path separator; path-prefixed docs are excluded from unauthenticated reads even in a public dataset. scripts/fix-dotted-ids.ts recreates documents under clean IDs and rewrites every _ref in the same transaction.
nodes.source_location: ### Never put a dot in a document `_id`

nodes.label: On-demand invalidation (SanityLive + /api/revalidate)
nodes.rationale: cacheLife uses Sanity's one-year profile in next.config.ts because updates are already pushed by <SanityLive /> for open sessions and the /api/revalidate webhook for everyone else; time-based expiry is unnecessary.

nodes.label: Rendering and caching (cacheComponents)
nodes.rationale: Published visitors take a synchronous path and get a fully prerendered page; only draft-mode requests pay for the cookie read.

nodes.label: Seeding (scripts/seed.ts, idempotent one-time migration)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic _ids written with createOrReplace in one transaction make the seed idempotent, and therefore destructive once real editing has started; delete scripts/legacy and seed.ts after it has run everywhere. Post bodies and images cannot be recovered because they never existed.

nodes.label: Type generation (hand-written types.ts vs generated sanity.types.ts)
nodes.norm_label: type generation (hand-written types.ts vs generated sanity.types.ts)
nodes.rationale: Two type sources deliberately: hand-written types.ts keeps prop types readable and compiles without a generator; sanity.types.ts from typegen is the authority. Reconciliation is manual because Portable Text is nominal in @portabletext/react but structural in typegen, so a mechanical assertion would false-positive on every rich-text type.

nodes.label: appendRow (writes header row on first use)
nodes.norm_label: appendrow (writes header row on first use)

nodes.label: safe (formula-injection guard)
nodes.rationale: Google Sheets treats cells starting with =, +, -, @ as formulas; a form field could plant a live formula that exfiltrates rows. A leading apostrophe forces literal text.

nodes.label: Google Apps Script Web App (Code.gs)
nodes.rationale: Spreadsheet IDs are read from Script Properties (SUBSCRIBE_SHEET_ID, QUOTE_SHEET_ID, AUDIT_SHEET_ID) rather than source because the repo is public. Deployed as Web app, execute as Me, access Anyone; sheets shared as Restricted.

nodes.label: GOOGLE_SHEETS_WEBHOOK_URL env var
nodes.rationale: No NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix so the /exec URL stays server-side only.

nodes.label: Form payload shapes and source values
nodes.norm_label: form payload shapes and source values

nodes.label: SubmissionThrottledError (403/429 mapping)
nodes.rationale: Forms say 'wait a few minutes' instead of 'something went wrong', because a generic error invites an immediate retry that spends more of the same rate-limit budget.

nodes.label: Form submissions to Google Sheets
nodes.rationale: The five public forms POST to app/api/forms/route.ts which forwards server-side to a Google Apps Script Web App, so the webhook URL never ships to the browser.

nodes.label: Vercel Firewall rate limit on /api/forms (30 POSTs / 600s)
nodes.norm_label: vercel firewall rate limit on /api/forms (30 posts / 600s)
nodes.rationale: Enforced at the edge so blocked requests leave no runtime log and return Vercel's error envelope. All five forms share one path and one per-IP counter; the original 5/600s limit was exhausted by retries and by visitors sharing a CGNAT/office NAT IP, which made legitimate submissions fail.
